title: Rollout Stoplight Decision Tree & Economic Sentinel
body:
Purpose:
This doc defines a compact, operational stoplight decision tree for staged feature rollouts plus an 'Economic Sentinel' — a thin cost-monitoring layer that gates traffic expansion when unit economics deviate. Intention is to give on-call, product ops, and platform a single rubric (green/amber/red) tied to both SLOs and per-token cost impact.

Context and why this is different:
- We often gate on latency/errors only. That misses cost regressions (quantization changes, batch policy shifts, model swaps) that can double run costs unnoticed.
- The stoplight combines reliability + cost + quality signals into a single pass/fail-ish decision tree so non-ML folks can make go/no-go calls during launches.

Quick summary of the decision tree (high level):
1) Green path: All primary SLOs within thresholds AND Economic sentinel below soft threshold -> expand to next stage.
2) Amber path: Any single SLO near threshold OR economic sentinel between soft and hard threshold -> hold expansion, start mitigation playbook, notify engineering and product ops.
3) Red path: Any SLO breach OR economic sentinel above hard threshold -> immediate rollback to last known stable model/version and trigger incident runbook.

Stoplight signal definitions (operationalizable):
- Latency SLO: 95th p90 token latency (in ms) for production routes. GREEN < 220ms, AMBER 220-300ms, RED > 300ms.
- Error rate: 5xx or model-inference-failures. GREEN < 0.15%, AMBER 0.15-0.5%, RED > 0.5%.
- Quality regressions: ASSESS via eval set pass-rate (synthetic prompt battery). GREEN >= 98% pass, AMBER 95-97%, RED < 95%. Note: quick eval run every stage; slower deep eval in parallel.
- Economic Sentinel (per-request unit economics): compute rolling 1h median of cost-per-1k-tokens (all-inference). SOFT ALARM if cost increases > 20% vs baseline for 1h; HARD ALARM if > 60% for 30m.

Decision logic examples (realistic scenarios):
- New quantization profile deployed: latency down but cost up 35% (Economic Sentinel enters SOFT). Result -> AMBER: pause increase, revert quantization for critical routes, run per-model profiling (owner: infra-quant).
- Canary shows higher hallucination rate on niche prompts while p95 latency fine: RED on quality -> immediate rollback to stable model, postmortem required.

Monitoring & dashboards to consult (quick list):
- Console > Rollouts > Stoplight (aggregated stoplight tile)
- Console > Cost > Per-model unit economics (1h and 24h views)
- Observability: traces (route-level), embeddings drift index (product-ops dashboard)
- Eval harness: /internal/evals/canary-suite results (automated after each deploy)

Escalation playbook (short):
- AMBER: 1) Create incident stub with tag "amber-rolling-hold"; 2) Notify #launch-ops and oncall infra; 3) Run mitigations checklist (see checklist item list) and wait 30–60m for stabilization; 4) If unresolved, escalate to Red.
- RED: 1) Trigger rollback; 2) Notify execs (product + eng leads) with short TL;DR; 3) Start postmortem template, assign SLO and cost owners; 4) Hotfix if problem isolated and regression fix < 2h, else revert and ramp down traffic to safe baseline.

Ownership & RACI (short):
- Product Ops (Maya) — decision authority for gating expansion during business hours.
- Serving Runtime (Jonah) — technical owner for latency/throughput regressions and rollbacks.
- Applied ML (Priya) — quality regressions and eval analysis.
- Infra/Cost (Luca) — investigate economic sentinel alerts and recommend config rollbacks.

Sprint cadence notes (how to use during rollout):
- Stage 0 (internal canary): 1% traffic for 2h, automated smoke and eval pass.
- Stage 1 (beta): 5% for 4h, verify stoplight green for sequential windows.
- Stage 2 (gradual ramp): 25% over 12h with checkpoints every 3h.
- Stage 3 (full): 100% after 24h of sustained green and economic sentinel stable.

What to capture in the incident stub (minimum):
- stage, stoplight color, primary violated signal, short numeric snapshot (p95 latency, error rate, cost % change), immediate mitigation attempted, roll-forward/rollback decision, owner actions.

Notes-to-self / unresolved questions:
- Need a compact synthetic eval set for fast canary quality checks that covers LLM hallucination + safety edge cases (Priya to propose a 50-prompt set).
- How to attribute cost spikes causally when there are concurrent infra batch changes? Luca to work on a causal detection ticket.
- Add a green-amber-red traffic-automation hook to the console to auto-hold expansion when amber threshold persists > 45m. (UX + legal review required.)

Appendix: Communication templates (short snippets)
- Amber alert message: "Amber hold on {feature}. Stoplight triggered by {signal}. Holding at current stage for mitigation. Owners: {names}. See console tile: {link}."
- Red alert message: "RED: rolling back {feature} to {stable-ref}. Primary issue: {signal}. Incident stub: {link}. Triage owners: {names}."

End of doc. This should be kept intentionally compact — transfer long playbooks to the ops-runbook repo and link here.
checklist: Pre-launch: confirm baseline unit economics snapshot (1d and 7d medians)
Create canary eval set and verify automated run completes within 10m
Set stoplight thresholds in Console; verify alerting routes to #launch-ops
Assign owners for latency, quality, and cost investigations
Verify rollback artifacts exist and are tested (model pinned + infra version)
Stage 0: run internal canary for 2h and validate stoplight is green
Stage 1: hold 5% beta, confirm economic sentinel under soft threshold
Document all mitigation steps attempted in incident stub
kpi_targets: Unit economics delta: soft alarm > +20% vs baseline, hard alarm > +60%
Cost per 1k tokens: monitor 1h median and 24h median for drift
owners: Oncall SRE — first responder for RED alerts
